client_side: clients.jsonl times are the capture script's own time.monotonic_ns, not the server's

trace_clock.name: time.monotonic_ns (clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC))
trace_clock.used_by: observability.py event durations (wait_ns, hold_ns, duration_ns, latency_ns, send_ns)

notes: asserted before writing: the oversize send was read by more than one conn.recv with the first exactly 1024 bytes, and a PRINT reply longer than 1024 bytes reached the client in more than one chunk (the client's first read after PRINT is exactly 1024 bytes and the rest arrives on a later read)

merged-sends probe (a second server run, two sendall calls back to back with no read in between): observed once, one conn.recv held both payloads; trace-merged.jsonl and clients-merged.jsonl are included. It ran once; it was never retried
attempt 1 of this scenario; a scenario without its behavior writes nothing, and a rerun is recorded as a higher attempt
the server's stdout and stderr go to the null device; it is stopped with SIGINT, so every trace ends with server.stop

power.source: Windows host through WSL interop: PowerStatus.PowerLineStatus; powercfg.exe /getactivescheme

timer.name: time.perf_counter_ns (clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC))
timer.overhead_note: not subtracted; one command round trip takes tens of microseconds or more

workload.print: one PRINT, one recv(1024), then GET k00 and reads until quiet
